# mokume — Full Reference

> Python library for protein quantification from peptide-level data.

## Overview

mokume takes peptide-level quantification data (from quantms, MaxQuant, DIA-NN, etc.) and computes protein-level abundances using various methods. It supports a plugin architecture for registering custom quantification methods.

## Installation

pip install mokume

## CLI Usage

### Basic protein quantification
mokume features2proteins -p peptides.parquet -o proteins.csv -s sdrf.tsv --quant-method ibaq

### Available quantification methods
mokume features2proteins --help

Methods: ibaq, topn, top3, top5, maxlfq, directlfq, ratio, sum, median

### With normalization and batch correction
mokume features2proteins -p peptides.parquet -o proteins.csv -s sdrf.tsv \
  --quant-method ibaq \
  --normalize median \
  --batch-correction combat

## Python API

### Basic quantification
from mokume.pipeline.features_to_proteins import PipelineConfig, QuantificationPipeline

config = PipelineConfig(
    parquet_path="peptides.parquet",
    sdrf_path="sdrf.tsv",
    quant_method="ibaq",
    output_path="proteins.csv"
)
pipeline = QuantificationPipeline(config)
result = pipeline.run()

### Using QpxDataset
from mokume.core.dataset import QpxDataset

# Load data
ds = QpxDataset.from_parquet("peptides.parquet")

# Access levels
peptides_df = ds.get_level("peptides")
proteins_df = ds.get_level("proteins")

# Save
ds.save("output_dir/")

# Lazy loading (DuckDB-backed)
ds = QpxDataset.from_parquet_lazy("large_dataset.parquet")

### Plugin Registry
from mokume.core.registry import PluginRegistry

# List available methods
methods = PluginRegistry.available("quantification")

# Get a method
method = PluginRegistry.get("quantification", "ibaq")

# Register custom method
@PluginRegistry.register("quantification", "my_method")
class MyMethod(QuantificationMethod):
    ...

## Quantification Methods

### iBAQ (Intensity-Based Absolute Quantification)
Divides summed peptide intensity by number of theoretically observable peptides. Requires protein FASTA for in-silico digestion.

### TopN
Uses top N most intense peptides per protein. Default N=3 (Top3). Configurable: top5, top10, etc.

### DirectLFQ
Integration with DirectLFQ algorithm for label-free quantification.

### MaxLFQ
MaxLFQ algorithm for delayed normalization of label-free data.

### Ratio
Log2 ratio-based quantification for TMT multiplexed experiments. Computes log2(sample/reference) per plex, with options for batch correction.

### Sum / Median
Simple aggregation methods: sum or median of peptide intensities per protein.

## Normalization Methods

- median: Median centering per sample
- quantile: Quantile normalization across samples
- tmm: Trimmed Mean of M-values
- irs: Internal Reference Scaling (for multi-plex TMT)

## Batch Correction

- combat: ComBat batch correction (parametric or non-parametric)

## Input Formats

- Parquet files (QPX format from qpx, or any Parquet with required columns)
- Required columns: ProteinName, PeptideSequence, SampleID, Intensity
- SDRF file for sample metadata

## Output Formats

- CSV: protein abundance matrix
- AnnData (h5ad): for integration with scanpy/single-cell tools
- QpxDataset: hierarchical container with metadata

## Flow Dispatch

mokume automatically selects the correct processing flow based on the quantification method:
- peptides level (iBAQ, TopN, MaxLFQ, sum, median): standard flow
- PSMs level (ratio): ratio flow for TMT
- peptides_raw level (DirectLFQ): DirectLFQ flow

## Troubleshooting

- "Unknown quantification method": check PluginRegistry.available("quantification")
- Memory issues with large datasets: use QpxDataset.from_parquet_lazy() for DuckDB-backed loading
- Missing columns: ensure input Parquet has ProteinName, PeptideSequence, SampleID, Intensity

## Related Tools

- quantms: DDA proteomics pipeline (https://docs.quantms.org)
- quantmsdiann: DIA proteomics pipeline (https://quantmsdiann.quantms.org)
- qpx: data format toolkit (https://qpx.quantms.org)
- pmultiqc: QC reports (https://pmultiqc.quantms.org)

## Citation

Zheng P et al. J Proteomics. 2025;317:105440. DOI: 10.1016/j.jprot.2025.105440
